_draft: Rivals / AI racers lane law. DRAFT — kept in a separate file so it can be written while the rails cycle is running against PHYSICS_GATES.json. Merge the `gates` array into references/PHYSICS_GATES.json when the rails lane settles, then build harness/rival-runner.mjs and harness/rival-mutants.mjs BEFORE any builder starts.
_designNotes: THE CENTRAL RULE: rivals ride the SAME physics as the player. They produce an INPUT each frame (the same {steer, tuck, boost, crouch, jumpRelease, spin, flip, grab, uber} shape the keyboard produces) and nothing else. A rival that writes velocity, position or heading directly is not a racer, it is a cutscene. This is the rivals-lane equivalent of the rails lane's GR-07/GR-11 and it is the gate most worth mutation-testing first.

SSX Tricky's AI is openly rubber-banded. The bar is not 'no catch-up' but 'catch-up you cannot see': bounded, off when the rival is ahead, and never expressed as raw speed the physics would not allow.
Every gate below must be reproducible from a seed. A flaky rival gate is worse than no gate — it trains everyone to re-run until green.

gates.statement: A rival drives the ACCEPTED physics through INPUTS ONLY. Replaying the rival's recorded input stream through a fresh createPhysics reproduces its trajectory to within 1e-6 m. Any direct write to pos/vel/heading makes this diverge immediately
gates._why: The whole lane is worthless if rivals cheat physics. Mutant: have the module nudge ps.pos[0] by 0.01 once per second.

gates.statement: Rival inputs stay inside the PLAYER'S input domain: steer/spin/flip in [-1,1], booleans actually boolean, uber in 1..6. No rival may pass a value the keyboard cannot produce
gates._why: steer: 3.0 is the cheapest possible cheat and looks like nothing in a trace.

gates.statement: Every rival FINISHES. Across 8 seeds and 4 rivals, all 32 runs reach zFinish without getting stuck, reversing permanently, or leaving the course
gates._why: A stuck rival is the single most visible AI failure. 32 runs, not 1 — a single lucky seed proves nothing.

gates.statement: Rivals stay in bounds: max lateral excursion beyond the course halfWidth is 0 m over every run in AI-03's matrix

Rubber-banding is BOUNDED and one-directional: any catch-up assistance is off while the rival leads the player, and the assisted-to-unassisted finish-time ratio never exceeds 1.15. Measured by running the same seed with assistance forced off
gates._why: Tricky rubber-bands and so should we. The gate is on the SIZE and the SIGN, not the existence. Mutant: apply catch-up while ahead.

gates.statement: Catch-up is expressed through INPUTS or declared physics parameters, never as a raw speed grant: a rival's instantaneous speed never exceeds what the accepted physics permits for its state (V_CAP, and V_BOOST while its own meter has charge)
The easy tier is BEATABLE: a reference mid-skill player run (the harness' scripted racer) finishes ahead of every easy rival across 8 seeds
The hard tier can WIN: the same reference mid-skill run finishes behind at least one hard rival across 8 seeds. A lane where the player always wins has no rivals in it
gates._why: AI-07 and AI-08 must BOTH hold. Either alone is trivially satisfiable by making the AI uniformly slow or uniformly fast.

gates.statement: Tiers are ORDERED and separated: mean finish time easy > medium > hard across 8 seeds, with each gap at least 3% of the course time. Overlapping tiers are indistinguishable to a player

Rivals RIDE, they do not rail the centreline: across a run each rival accumulates real airtime on the course's kickers (>= 1.5 s total) and its lateral track deviates from the exact centreline (RMS >= 2 m). A rival pinned to the centre line reads as a moving cone
gates._why: Written as PRESENCE of both behaviours so it cannot pass by absence — the failure this lane will actually produce is a perfect centreline follower.

gates.statement: Rivals are DETERMINISTIC given a seed: two runs with the same seed produce byte-identical finish times and identical input streams
gates._why: Without this every other gate in this file is flaky and will be re-run until green.

gates.statement: Rivals do not interpenetrate the player or each other: minimum centre-to-centre separation over a full race is >= 0.6 m, and no rival remains within 1.0 m of the player for more than 2.0 s (no shepherding, no blocking-lock)
PERFORMANCE: 5 rivals plus the player sustain 60 fps in the rig, and the rivals' own update costs <= 1.5 ms/frame measured separately from render

_mutantsToWriteFirst: AI-01: nudge ps.pos[0] += 0.01 once per second — replay must diverge
AI-02: emit steer: 3.0 on one frame
AI-03: freeze one rival's input after 20 s — finishRate must drop
AI-05: apply catch-up while the rival is AHEAD
AI-06: grant +8 m/s directly when behind
AI-08: make the hard tier 20% slower — hardTierWins must fail
AI-09: set all three tiers to the same parameters
AI-10: pin the rival exactly to the centreline — must fail on BOTH clauses
AI-11: seed the rival RNG from Date.now()
_openQuestions: Does the player collide with rivals, or pass through them? Collision is a physics-contract change (the accepted physics has no rider-rider term) and is a USER DECISION, not a builder's. AI-12 is written as a separation measurement so it holds either way.
Tricky's rivals also trick and build boost. Deferred: this draft races them only. Adding trick behaviour means rivals drive the trick system too, which is a second lane.
